text:
sam: FYI rolling /merge 2731 seems to have triggered a 95p latency regression on canary. CI perf job failed: perf/latency-95 climbed from ~85ms -> ~210ms. Seeing correlations with longer seqs and high batch sizes. :frowning:

maya: link to the CI run? did the synthetic suite catch this? :eyes:

liam: CI: https://ci.redwood/proj/2731/build/1123 — perf-regress-ci flagged it. Error summary shows tail latency spike when qlen>8 (batch window increase + kv prefetch changes in 2731).

jordana: quick profile from canary nodes attached — main hotspot is kv_lookup + batch_assemble. snippet:
```
kv_lookup: 42% samples, median 12ms, p95 78ms
batch_assemble: 31% samples, waits on kv miss paths
net_io: 10%
```

kevin: interesting — PR 2731 bumped batch build window from 8ms -> 20ms and enabled aggressive prefetch TTL reset. I think when KV miss rate > ~0.15 this increases concurrent KV churn and creates tail spikiness.

sam: can we bisect to the exact commit in 2731? if it's the batching change we should revert that part.

liam: ran bisect between base..2731, pinpointed commit 2731^5 (batch-window change) as the regression. Reproduces locally with the canary workload: `make perf-local PROFILE=longseq-kv` returns same p95 bump.

maya: short-term options: (1) rollback full PR on canary, (2) patch to cap batch window when kv_miss_rate > 0.2, (3) gate rollout with stricter SLO checks so autopause triggers. Thoughts?

jordana: do manual rollback on canary now, then iterate on a conservative patch. If we leave it live the canary fraction could cause customer impact when we scale.

kevin: +1. I'll run the rollback. /release rollback 2731 --env=canary

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: rollback-2187659000-1 (user: kevin). Starting canary rollback...

ops-bot: Metric alert suppressed for rollback window.

sam: after rollback metrics: p95 back down to ~90ms within 5m of rollback. Looks like batch-window delta is root cause. :thumbsup:

liam: created issue PERF-1048 to add a CI synthetic that combines long sequences + low KV hit to catch this in perf-regress-ci. Also adding an integration test asserting p95 change < 15% on merge.

maya: long term we should: - tighten the canary SLO gate (fail if p95 rises >12% over baseline) - implement adaptive batching: cap window when kv_miss_rate high - add KV miss-aware prefetch backoff. I'll draft a proposal.

jordana: one gotcha — adaptive cap should still allow larger batches for short-seq workloads. Suggest using weighted heuristic: cap = f(hit_rate, avg_seq_len).

kevin: thanks everyone. Action items: I rolled back canary (done), liam opening PERF-1048 + CI test, maya will draft adaptive batching RFC, jordana will add regression note to PR template. We'll keep canary at 0% until patch lands.

sam: reassigning follow-ups in the incident board. Closing thread once RFC posted. :white_check_mark:
